chunks: We have made whatever is on the earth as adornment for it, to test them [as to] which of them is best in deed.
ai.seo_question: What is the purpose of worldly wealth and beauty according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Kahf is often interpreted as a test of spiritual prioritization, where 'best in deed' (ahsanu amalan) refers not merely to quantity but to the quality and sincerity of one's actions amidst worldly distractions. The material adornment (zīnah) serves as a temporary trial to distinguish those who utilize wealth for divine purposes from those who are consumed by it. This perspective emphasizes that true success lies in maintaining taqwa (God-consciousness) while navigating the allure of the dunya.
